title: Samtskhe-Saatabago
capsule: Samtskhe-Saatabago was a Georgian feudal principality in the southern Caucasus, centered on the Samtskhe region (modern Javakheti and Meskheti) and ruled by the Jaqeli family as hereditary atabegs. Kvarkvare II Jaqeli formally broke from the Kingdom of Georgia in 1465, defeating King George VIII near Lake Paravani and cementing the principality's independence amid the fragmentation of the medieval Georgian realm. Through the late fifteenth century the principality faced repeated incursions by the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen (notably in 1466, 1476-77, and 1485) and growing Ottoman pressure from 1479 onward, even as Kvarkvare himself raided as far as Erzurum. Under his successors Kaikhosro I (1498-1500) and Mzetchabuk (1500-1515), Samtskhe persisted as a contested borderland between the Georgian kingdoms and rising powers in Anatolia and Persia.
